title: Generic syntax error
description: The parser encountered a syntax error that doesn't fit other categories.

title: Missing node (syntax error)
description: The parser encountered a syntax error — a required element is missing.
sources:
NAMESPACE
END_NAMESPACE

title: Variable type is missing
description: Every variable declaration must have a type annotation.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unexpected variable initialization
description: Variable initialization is not allowed in this context.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR_IN_OUT
    x : INT := 5;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Empty right-hand side of assignment
description: The right-hand side of an assignment cannot be empty.

title: Invalid assignment sign '='
description: Use `:=` for assignment, not `=`.

title: Invalid assignment sign ':'
description: Use `:=` for assignment, not `:`.

title: Invalid assignment sign '=>' in assignment
description: Use `:=` for assignment, not `=>`. The `=>` operator is for output parameters in function calls.

title: Invalid assignment sign '=' in FOR list
description: Use `:=` for FOR loop initialization, not `=`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    i: INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i = 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Invalid assignment sign ':' in FOR list
description: Use `:=` for FOR loop initialization, not `:`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    i: INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i : 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Invalid assignment sign '=>' in FOR list
description: Use `:=` for FOR loop initialization, not `=>`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    i: INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i => 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Assignment sign ':=' in a condition
description: A condition compares, so it takes `=`. `:=` assigns, and writing one where the language expects a test is almost always a typo for the other.

title: Assignment to function call
description: You cannot assign a value to a function call expression.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1 : INT END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    fn1() := 5;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Incomplete edge qualifier
description: An edge qualifier like `R_` or `F_ED` was started but not completed. Use `R_EDGE` or `F_EDGE`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR_INPUT
    x : BOOL R_ED;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: THIS used as a path member
description:
`THIS` may only start a path expression (`THIS.member`, `THIS^.member`).

It is not a member name, so it cannot appear after a dot.

Using `THIS` in a POU that has no instance — a FUNCTION — is reported as E1105 instead.

title: SUPER after a dot in a path
description:
`SUPER` must be the first element of a path expression, as in `SUPER.m()`.

It cannot appear as a member after a dot — `THIS.SUPER.m()` and `inst.SUPER.x` are rejected.

(Using a correctly placed `SUPER` in a POU with no EXTENDS clause is E1107; using it in a POU that cannot extend at all, such as a FUNCTION, is E1106.)
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
METHOD m
END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
    THIS.SUPER.m();
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR not allowed in this context
description: `VAR` can only be used inside FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, or PROGRAM.
sources:
CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    VAR

    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: VAR_IN_OUT not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_IN_OUT` can only be used inside FUNCTION and FUNCTION_BLOCK.
sources:
CLASS c1
    VAR_IN_OUT

    END_VAR
END_CLASS

title: VAR_TEMP not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_TEMP` can only be used inside FUNCTION and FUNCTION_BLOCK.
sources:
CLASS c1
    VAR_TEMP

    END_VAR
END_CLASS

title: VAR_EXTERNAL not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_EXTERNAL` can only be used inside PROGRAM, FUNCTION_BLOCK, or FUNCTION.
sources:
INTERFACE in
    METHOD m
        VAR_EXTERNAL

        END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

title: VAR_GLOBAL not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_GLOBAL` can only be used inside a CONFIGURATION. Global data is application-scoped: a POU reaches it with `VAR_EXTERNAL`, and a RESOURCE holds no variables of its own.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    VAR_GLOBAL

    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR_ACCESS not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_ACCESS` can only be used inside PROGRAM.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    VAR_ACCESS

    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR_CONFIG not allowed in this context
description: `VAR_CONFIG` can only be used inside CONFIGURATION.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    VAR_CONFIG

    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: PROGRAM not allowed in namespace
description: PROGRAM declarations cannot appear inside a NAMESPACE.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    PROGRAM p1
    END_PROGRAM
END_NAMESPACE

title: CONFIGURATION not allowed in namespace
description: CONFIGURATION declarations cannot appear inside a NAMESPACE.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    CONFIGURATION c1
    END_CONFIGURATION
END_NAMESPACE

title: Variable declarations after methods (FB)
description: In a FUNCTION_BLOCK, variable declarations must appear before methods.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    VAR
        x: INT;
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Variable declarations after methods (CLASS)
description: In a CLASS, variable declarations must appear before methods.
sources:
CLASS c1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    VAR
        x: INT;
    END_VAR
END_CLASS

title: Method declaration in body
description: A METHOD declaration cannot appear inside the body (statement list) of a POU. Methods must be declared at the top level of a FUNCTION_BLOCK or CLASS.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x: INT;
END_VAR
    x := 1;
    METHOD m1
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Duplicate variable
description: Two variables in the same scope have the same name.

title: Duplicate POU
description: Two POUs (functions, function blocks, classes, etc.) have the same name.

title: Duplicate parameter
description: A function call passes the same parameter twice.

title: Duplicate struct field
description: Two fields in a STRUCT have the same name.

title: Duplicate enum variant
description: Two variants in an ENUM have the same name.
sources:
TYPE e1 : (Red, Green, Red)
END_TYPE

title: Duplicate field in initializer expression
description: A struct initializer assigns the same field twice.

title: Variable is the return value
description:
Inside a FUNCTION or a value-returning METHOD, the callable's own name is its return value, so a variable declared with that name (in any case: identifiers are not case sensitive) is a second declaration of it.

The body would bind to the local, at the local's type, while the signature still promises the return type's.

title: Duplicate method declaration
description: Two methods in the same POU have the same name.
sources:
CLASS c1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Duplicate method prototype
description: Two method prototypes in an interface have the same name.
sources:
INTERFACE i1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

title: Duplicate inherited method
description: Two interfaces implemented by the same POU define a method with the same name.
sources:
INTERFACE i1
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

INTERFACE i2
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS c1 IMPLEMENTS i1, i2
    METHOD m1 END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Duplicate USING namespace import
description: The same namespace is imported twice with `USING`.

title: Duplicate PROGRAM
description: Two PROGRAM declarations have the same name.
sources:
PROGRAM p1
END_PROGRAM

PROGRAM p1
END_PROGRAM

title: Duplicate PROGRAM instance name
description: Two PROGRAM instances in the same configuration have the same name.

title: Duplicate TASK name
description: Two TASKs in the same configuration have the same name.

title: Duplicate RESOURCE name
description: Two RESOURCE blocks in the same configuration have the same name.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(PRIORITY := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task2(PRIORITY := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: No item found in scope
description: A referenced name does not exist in the current scope.

title: No such field
description: The type has no field with the given name.

title: No namespace item found
description: The referenced item does not exist in the specified namespace path.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    FUNCTION fn1 : INT
        fn1 := 0;
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ns1.unknown;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: USING namespace not found
description: The namespace referenced in a `USING` directive does not exist.

title: Multiple items with same name in scope
description: Two or more items are available in scope with the same name, creating ambiguity.

title: External variable not found
description: A `VAR_EXTERNAL` declaration references a name not present in any accessible `VAR_GLOBAL`.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
VAR_EXTERNAL
    missing_global : INT;
END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH task1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: External variable type mismatch
description:
A VAR_EXTERNAL aliases its VAR_GLOBAL's storage by name, so the external must repeat the global's type exactly, subrange included.

A plain INT external over an INT (0..10) global would store around the range check.
sources:
TYPE Small : INT (0..10); END_TYPE

PROGRAM MyProg
    VAR_EXTERNAL
        g : INT;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    VAR_GLOBAL
        g : Small;
    END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : MyProg;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: RETAIN in a stateless POU
description: RETAIN and NON_RETAIN require instance storage. A FUNCTION or METHOD has none - its variables live for one call.
sources:
FUNCTION f1 : INT
VAR_OUTPUT RETAIN q : INT; END_VAR
    f1 := 1;
END_FUNCTION

title: Type mismatch
description: The types on both sides of an assignment or expression are incompatible.

title: Types not comparable
description: The two types cannot be compared with comparison operators.

title: Types not addable
description: The two types cannot be used with addition or subtraction operators.

title: Types not multiplicable
description: The two types cannot be used with multiplication or division operators.

title: Unsupported operator for type
description: The operator cannot be applied to this type.

title: Literal out of range
description: The literal is well-formed but outside what the type can hold. The message ends with the type's bounds.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    test: INT := 32768;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Negative literal for an unsigned type
description: A minus sign on a literal whose type has no negative values. Use the signed twin of the type, or drop the sign.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    test: UINT := -1;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Literal of the wrong kind
description: The literal is not the kind of value the type takes: a fraction where a whole number is expected, or a number where `TRUE` or `FALSE` is.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x: INT := 5.5;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed duration
description: A `TIME` or `LTIME` literal the compiler cannot read: a unit it does not know, a missing unit, or components out of order. A duration is written `T#1d2h3m4s5ms`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    t: TIME := T#5x;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed date
description: A `DATE` or `LDATE` literal with a month or day that does not exist, or the wrong shape. A date is written `D#2025-01-31`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    d: DATE := DATE#2024-13-45;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed time of day
description: A `TOD` or `LTOD` literal with an hour, minute or second that does not exist, or the wrong shape. A time of day is written `TOD#12:30:00.500`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    t: TOD := TOD#25:36:55.36;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Malformed date and time
description: A `DT` or `LDT` literal with a component that does not exist, or the wrong shape. A date and time is written `DT#2025-01-31-12:30:00`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    dt: DT := DT#1984-06-25-25:36:55.360;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: CHAR literal is not one character
description: A `CHAR` holds exactly one character. The literal has none, or more than one.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    c: CHAR := CHAR#'ab';
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: STRING literal exceeds its capacity
description: The literal is longer than the `STRING[n]` it is assigned to. Widen the declaration, or shorten the literal; nothing is truncated silently.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    s: STRING[2] := 'hello';
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: STRING length is not constant
description:
A `STRING[n]` length is part of the TYPE — it decides how many bytes the variable occupies — so it must be known at compile time.

It may name a CONSTANT, exactly as an array bound may; what it may not do is depend on something only the runtime knows.

Defaulting to 80 instead would size the storage wrongly and say nothing about it.

title: Function used as type
description: A FUNCTION cannot be used as a variable type or data type.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    fn1 := 0;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : fn1;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Direct type usage
description: A type name cannot be used directly as a value. Types are not first-class values.
sources:
TYPE b1 : INT
END_TYPE

FUNCTION fn1
    VAR_OUTPUT
        param1: INT;
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    fn1(param1 => b1);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Assignment to a function block instance
description:
A variable whose declared type is callable — a FUNCTION_BLOCK instance, or a name that resolves to a FUNCTION — cannot be the target of an assignment.

Instances are called, not copied; pass one as a VAR_IN_OUT parameter, or assign its individual members.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb2
VAR
    inst : fb1;
END_VAR
    inst := 0;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Initial value is not constant
description:
A TYPE default, an FB/CLASS member default, and a static initializer (a PROGRAM field, a config VAR_GLOBAL) are part of a declaration, fixed before the program runs — so the value must be a constant.

A CONSTANT reference folds; a reference to an ordinary variable has no one value to fold to.

FUNCTION locals are exempt: they re-initialize on every call and may compute their value.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb
VAR
    m : DINT := some_global;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL
    some_global : DINT := 5;
END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : Dummy;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

PROGRAM Dummy
VAR t : INT; END_VAR
    t := 0;
END_PROGRAM

title: Function call in initialization expression
description: Function calls are not allowed in variable initialization expressions.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    ml : ARRAY [0..2] OF INT := [1(call(IN := 5, OUT => OUT))];
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Elementary type initialized with parentheses
description: Elementary types like INT, BOOL, REAL cannot be initialized with `()`
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : INT := ();
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Assignment to constant
description: Cannot assign to a variable declared as CONSTANT.

title: Invalid array lower bound
description: The lower bound of an array declaration is not a valid constant value.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[TRUE..5] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Invalid array upper bound
description: The upper bound of an array declaration is not a valid constant value.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[0..TRUE] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Upper bound must be greater than lower bound
description: In an array declaration, the upper bound must be greater than the lower bound.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[10..0] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Array index must be an integer
description: A subscript must be of an integer type (ANY_INT; subranges index like their base type). A BOOL, REAL or STRING cannot address an element.

title: Invalid array index value
description: An array initializer repeat count is not a valid integer value (e.g., overflow).
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[0..2] OF INT := [99999999999999999999(0)];
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Constant index out of bounds
description: A constant subscript outside the array's declared bounds is provable at compile time and rejected here, instead of faulting the scan at runtime. Checked per dimension.

title: Too many elements in array initializer
description: The array initializer provides more elements than the declared array size.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    x : ARRAY[0..1] OF INT := [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Index into non-array type
description: Array indexing can only be used on ARRAY types.

title: Array conformands not supported
description: Array conformands (`ARRAY[*]`) are not supported.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
VAR_INPUT
    x : ARRAY[*] OF INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Invalid enum type
description: Only numeric integer types are allowed for ENUM base types.
sources:
TYPE e1 : REAL (Red, Green, Blue)
END_TYPE

title: Not an ENUM type
description:
The `#` enum access syntax was used on a name that does not denote an ENUM — a non-ENUM type name, or a variable whose type is not an ENUM.

Elementary type keywords (`INT#16`, `BOOL#TRUE`) are typed literals, a separate syntax that never reaches this check.
sources:
TYPE MyInt : INT; END_TYPE

FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    fn1 := MyInt#Red;
END_FUNCTION

title: ENUM variant not found
description: The referenced variant does not exist on this ENUM type.
sources:
TYPE Color : (Red, Green, Blue) END_TYPE

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    c : Color;
END_VAR
    c := Color#Yellow;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: ENUM variant value is not a constant
description:
A declared variant value fixes the variant's ordinal, so it must evaluate to a constant at compile time.

A literal, a named CONSTANT and arithmetic over those all fold; a call or an ordinary variable does not.
sources:
FUNCTION f1 : INT
END_FUNCTION

TYPE Mode : (Idle := f1(), Run) END_TYPE

title: Invalid subrange type
description: Only numeric integer types are allowed for subrange types.
sources:
TYPE s1 : REAL (0..100)
END_TYPE

title: Value outside the subrange
description: A constant assigned to a subrange-typed variable must lie within the declared bounds.

title: Subrange bound is not a constant
description: A subrange's bounds are part of the type, so each must evaluate to a constant at compile time. A named CONSTANT and folding arithmetic are fine; an ordinary variable is not.

title: Subrange mismatch across a reference
description:
A VAR_IN_OUT argument or an output destination binds the callee to the caller's storage by reference, so both ends must agree about the subrange.

A callee writing through a plain INT would otherwise go around the range check of the caller's INT (0..10).

title: Incorrect number of function parameters
description: A function call passes more or fewer parameters than expected.

title: Missing required parameter
description: A FUNCTION call must supply every VAR_INPUT (inputs have no defaults on FUNCTIONs). Name the missing parameter in the call.
sources:
FUNCTION add2 : INT
VAR_INPUT a : INT; b : INT; END_VAR
    add2 := a + b;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION f1 : INT
    f1 := add2(a := 1);
END_FUNCTION

title: Unknown input parameter
description: A named input parameter does not exist on the called function.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Motor
VAR_INPUT
    u: BOOL;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    m: Motor;
END_VAR
    m(unknown := TRUE);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unknown output parameter
description: A named output parameter does not exist on the called function.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
VAR_OUTPUT
    o: BOOL;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
VAR
    b: BOOL;
END_VAR
    fn1(unknown => b);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Output parameter used as input
description: A VAR_OUTPUT parameter cannot be used as a positional (non-formal) input.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
    VAR_INPUT
        a: INT;
    END_VAR
    VAR_OUTPUT
        b: INT;
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    fn1(1, 2);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: VAR_IN_OUT argument must be a variable
description: A VAR_IN_OUT parameter is passed by reference: the argument must be an assignable variable, not an expression or a literal.

title: VAR_IN_OUT bound with =>
description: The `=>` arrow binds outputs. A VAR_IN_OUT parameter is bound with `:=` - it flows both ways through one variable.
sources:
FUNCTION bump : INT
VAR_IN_OUT io : INT; END_VAR
    bump := io;
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION f1 : INT
VAR y : INT; END_VAR
    f1 := bump(io => y);
END_FUNCTION

title: Call non-callable type
description: Attempting to call something that is not a function or instantiated function block.

title: Ambiguous overloaded call
description:
A call matches more than one FUNCTION overload and no overload is an exact match for every argument, so the compiler refuses to guess.

Disambiguate with a typed literal or an explicit conversion (e.g. `DINT#5`).

title: No overload accepts the arguments
description:
The call names an overloaded FUNCTION and none of its overloads accepts the argument types.

The first overload used to stand in and report its own parameter mismatch, so the message named a type nobody wrote, such as expected 'CHAR', got 'DATE' for a date assertion.

Each overload and what it accepts is listed.

title: Non-variadic type for variable
description: Only elementary types can be declared as variadic (`...`). Structs and other composite types cannot.
sources:
TYPE MyStruct :
    STRUCT
        field1: INT;
    END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

FUNCTION sum_all : INT
    VAR_INPUT
        args: MyStruct...
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Multiple variadic variables
description: Only one variadic parameter is allowed per POU.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1
    VAR_INPUT
        a: INT...
        b: INT...
    END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Variadic call without arguments
description: A variadic parameter must receive at least one argument. A fold such as `...args+` has no value over an empty pack, so an empty call has nothing to compute.
sources:
FUNCTION sum_all : INT
    VAR_INPUT
        args: INT...
    END_VAR
    sum_all := ...args+
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    fn1 := sum_all()
END_FUNCTION

title: Non-variadic fold parameter
description: The `...` fold operator can only be used on variadic parameters.
sources:
FUNCTION sum_all : INT
    VAR_INPUT
        args: INT
    END_VAR
    sum_all := ...args+
END_FUNCTION

title: Variadic parameter beside other inputs
description: A variadic parameter takes every argument of the call, so it must be the only `VAR_INPUT` parameter.
sources:
FUNCTION fn1 : INT
VAR_INPUT
    x: INT;
    args: INT...
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Dereference of non-reference type
description: The `^` dereference operator can only be used on `REF_TO` types.

title: Possibly null dereference
description: Dereferencing a reference that may be null or uninitialized.

title: Reference outlives its storage
description:
A FUNCTION or METHOD returned a reference to its own per-call storage.

That storage is reused by the next invocation, so the reference reads whatever that call leaves behind.

Return a reference to instance state, or to storage the caller owns (a VAR_IN_OUT).
sources:
TYPE PInt : REF_TO INT; END_TYPE

FUNCTION borrow : PInt
VAR
    local : INT := 1;
END_VAR
    borrow := REF(local);
END_FUNCTION

title: Cannot access PRIVATE item
description: PRIVATE items can only be accessed from within the same POU.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PRIVATE myPrivateMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Mid EXTENDS Base
    METHOD testMethod : INT
        SUPER.myPrivateMethod();
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Cannot access PROTECTED item
description: PROTECTED items can only be accessed within the same POU or derived POUs.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PROTECTED myProtectedMethod  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

FUNCTION_BLOCK fn1
    VAR
        obj: Base;
    END_VAR
    obj.myProtectedMethod();
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Cannot access INTERNAL item
description: INTERNAL items can only be accessed from within the same namespace.
sources:
NAMESPACE ns1
    CLASS Base
        METHOD INTERNAL myInternalMethod : INT  END_METHOD
    END_CLASS
END_NAMESPACE

NAMESPACE ns2
    USING ns1;

    CLASS Mid EXTENDS Base
        METHOD testMethod : INT
            SUPER.myInternalMethod();
        END_METHOD
    END_CLASS
END_NAMESPACE

title: Internal namespace accessed from outside
description:
A NAMESPACE INTERNAL is reachable only from inside the namespace that encloses it, nested namespaces included, on its own side of the library line.

A USING of one is refused at the USING.

At the top level the enclosing namespace is the root, so INTERNAL there means this library only.
sources:
NAMESPACE Lib
    NAMESPACE INTERNAL Impl
        FUNCTION hidden : INT
            hidden := 1;
        END_FUNCTION
    END_NAMESPACE
END_NAMESPACE

FUNCTION use : INT
    use := Lib.Impl.hidden();
END_FUNCTION

title: Private function called from outside its namespace
description: A FUNCTION declared PRIVATE is callable only from its own namespace, nested namespaces included, on its own side of the library line. An extension: the standard gives a FUNCTION no access specifier.
sources:
NAMESPACE Lib
    FUNCTION PRIVATE helper : INT
        helper := 1;
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

NAMESPACE App
    FUNCTION use : INT
        use := Lib.helper();
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

title: Specifier not applicable to a FUNCTION
description: Only PRIVATE applies to a FUNCTION (PUBLIC spells the default); PROTECTED and INTERNAL do not.

title: Cannot access test-only item
description: Items annotated with `{test}` can only be accessed from other test-annotated code.

title: Multiple EXTENDS declarations
description: A class or function block can only have one `EXTENDS` clause.
sources:
CLASS c1 EXTENDS c2 EXTENDS c3
END_CLASS

CLASS c2
END_CLASS

CLASS c3
END_CLASS

title: Multiple IMPLEMENTS declarations
description: A class or function block can only have one `IMPLEMENTS` clause. Combine all interfaces in a single `IMPLEMENTS` list.
sources:
INTERFACE a
END_INTERFACE

INTERFACE b
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK fn IMPLEMENTS a IMPLEMENTS b
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: IMPLEMENTS before EXTENDS
description: The `EXTENDS` clause must appear before `IMPLEMENTS`.
sources:
CLASS b
END_CLASS

FUNCTION_BLOCK fn IMPLEMENTS a EXTENDS b
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Extending a FINAL type
description: A CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK declared FINAL is complete and closed: it may be used, but not extended.
sources:
CLASS FINAL Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT  myMethod := 1; END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
END_CLASS

title: THIS not valid here
description: `THIS` is not valid in a FUNCTION context.

title: SUPER not valid here
description: `SUPER` is not valid in a POU that does not extend another.

title: SUPER but no EXTENDS clause
description: `SUPER` is used but the current POU has no `EXTENDS` clause.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK fb1
    SUPER.method1()
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: SUPER() body not valid here
description: `SUPER()` (body call) is not valid in this context.
sources:
CLASS fb1
    METHOD method1
        SUPER()
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: SUPER() called in a method
description: `SUPER()` (the base function-block body call) may only appear in the function block body, not in a method of a function block.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
    METHOD m1
        SUPER()
    END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: SUPER() called more than once
description: The call of `SUPER()` shall occur once in the function block body.

title: SUPER() called inside a loop
description: The call of `SUPER()` shall not be in a loop (`FOR`/`WHILE`/`REPEAT`).
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
    VAR i : INT; END_VAR
    FOR i := 1 TO 3 DO
        SUPER();
    END_FOR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Missing OVERRIDE keyword
description: When redefining a method from a base class, the OVERRIDE keyword is required.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Invalid OVERRIDE usage
description: OVERRIDE is only valid when a method with the same name exists in the base class.
sources:
CLASS Base
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Cannot override FINAL method
description: Methods marked as FINAL cannot be overridden in derived classes.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC FINAL myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Inherited variable name shadowed
description: The names of the variables in the base and the derived function blocks shall be unique. A derived function block may not redeclare a variable name inherited from a base.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK base
VAR c : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK derived EXTENDS base
VAR c : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Missing ABSTRACT method implementation
description: Derived POUs must implement all ABSTRACT methods from their base class.
sources:
CLASS ABSTRACT Base
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
END_CLASS

title: ABSTRACT method in a concrete POU
description: A CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK declaring an ABSTRACT method must itself be ABSTRACT.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Instantiation of an ABSTRACT type
description: An ABSTRACT CLASS or FUNCTION_BLOCK has no implementation of its own, so it cannot be instantiated. Declare a variable of a derived type instead.
sources:
CLASS ABSTRACT Base
    METHOD PUBLIC ABSTRACT myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_CLASS

PROGRAM Main
VAR
    b : Base;
END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Unimplemented interface method
description: A class implementing an interface must provide all required methods.
sources:
INTERFACE IMyInterface
    METHOD myMethod : INT  END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS MyClass IMPLEMENTS IMyInterface
END_CLASS

title: Access specifier on interface method prototype
description: Access specifiers (PUBLIC, PRIVATE, etc.) are not allowed on interface method prototypes. Interface methods are implicitly PUBLIC.
sources:
INTERFACE iface
    METHOD PUBLIC m1
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

title: Interface type only allowed as a parameter
description:
An interface type may appear only as a `VAR_INPUT` or `VAR_IN_OUT` parameter, where it is monomorphized to the concrete type passed by the caller.

It cannot be a stored `VAR`, member, `VAR_OUTPUT`, `VAR_TEMP`, or global.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

PROGRAM Main
    VAR
        dev : ITF1;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Interface not allowed as a return type
description: An interface may not be used as a function or method return type: the concrete type would flow from callee to caller and could not be resolved at compile time.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION Make : ITF1
END_FUNCTION

title: Interface not allowed nested in an aggregate
description:
An interface may not be nested inside an array, reference, or struct (e.g. `ARRAY OF ITF1`, `REF_TO ITF1`, or a struct field).

Such a placement is stored, heterogeneous state that cannot be monomorphized.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

PROGRAM Main
    VAR
        arr : ARRAY[0..2] OF ITF1;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

title: Assignment to an interface parameter
description:
An interface `VAR_IN_OUT` parameter is a fixed binding to the concrete type passed by the caller.

Reassigning it would break monomorphization (the body is specialized to one concrete type), so it can be used — methods called, passed on — but not reassigned.
sources:
INTERFACE ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

FUNCTION_BLOCK Impl IMPLEMENTS ITF1
    METHOD DoWork END_METHOD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION Use : INT
    VAR_IN_OUT dev : ITF1; END_VAR
    VAR other : Impl; END_VAR
    dev := other;
END_FUNCTION

title: Method parameter count mismatch
description:
A method implementing an interface prototype or overriding a base method declares a different number of parameters.

Parameters are matched by position; their names (E1128), sections (E1129) and types (E1126) and the return type (E1127) are checked one by one.
sources:
CLASS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC myMethod : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

CLASS Derived EXTENDS Base
    METHOD PUBLIC OVERRIDE myMethod : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; b : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method parameter type mismatch
description:
A parameter of a method implementing an interface prototype or overriding a base method has a different type than the parameter at the same position in the base.

Widening does not apply: a call through the base signature passes the base's type.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : REAL; END_VAR
        M := 0;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method return type mismatch
description:
A method implementing an interface prototype or overriding a base method declares a different return type, or a return type where the base has none.

A caller through the base signature reads the base's type.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : REAL
        M := 0.0;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method parameter name mismatch
description:
A parameter of a method implementing an interface prototype or overriding a base method has a different name than the parameter at the same position in the base.

Parameters are matched by position, and a caller binding a name through the base signature must reach the same parameter in the implementation.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT b : INT; END_VAR
        M := b;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: Method parameter section mismatch
description:
A parameter of a method implementing an interface prototype or overriding a base method is declared in a different section (VAR_INPUT, VAR_OUTPUT, VAR_IN_OUT) than in the base.

The section decides how the argument is passed: a VAR_INPUT prototype implemented as VAR_IN_OUT is called by value through the interface and by address in the implementation.
sources:
INTERFACE I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_INPUT a : INT; END_VAR
    END_METHOD
END_INTERFACE

CLASS C IMPLEMENTS I
    METHOD M : INT
        VAR_IN_OUT a : INT; END_VAR
        M := a;
    END_METHOD
END_CLASS

title: EXIT outside loop
description: `EXIT` can only be used inside a loop (FOR, WHILE, REPEAT).

title: CONTINUE outside loop
description: `CONTINUE` can only be used inside a loop (FOR, WHILE, REPEAT).

title: FOR control is not a variable
description: A FOR statement's control must be a bare variable name. A struct field, an array element, a dereference or a bit access cannot be a loop counter.

title: FOR step is not a nonzero constant
description:
The step's sign picks the loop's direction when the code is compiled, so the step must evaluate to a constant at compile time — and to a nonzero one, since a step of zero never advances the counter.

A CONSTANT variable or folding arithmetic works; an ordinary variable does not.

title: CASE label is not a constant
description:
A CASE label selects a branch at compile time, so its value cannot depend on anything computed while the program runs.

IEC's `Case_List_Elem` is a subrange or a `Constant_Expr` — any expression that evaluates to a constant before the program runs — so a literal, a string, an enum value, a named CONSTANT and arithmetic over those are all labels; an ordinary variable is not.

A label the compiler could not evaluate used to pass `rk check` and then abort `rk compile` with an internal compiler error.

title: Direct recursion
description: A type contains itself directly, creating infinite recursion.
sources:
TYPE s1 : STRUCT
    field1 : s1;
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

title: Mutual recursion
description: Two or more types reference each other, creating a recursive cycle.
sources:
TYPE a : STRUCT
    field1 : b;
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

TYPE b : STRUCT
    field1 : a;
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

title: No project configuration
description:
The workspace holds no config.toml, so nothing marks it as a project: its files are still checked, as loose sources, but no library is loaded and nothing can be compiled or deployed.

Create a config.toml with a [project] table (name and version), or point --workspace at the directory that has one.

This is about the workspace rather than a file, so no source example can show it.

title: More than one CONFIGURATION
description:
A workspace declares one CONFIGURATION.

A POU is a type any configuration may use, so with two of them there is no answer to which global variables are in scope inside a POU.

Describe another PLC in its own workspace.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION cfg1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

CONFIGURATION cfg2
    RESOURCE res2 ON CPU
        TASK t2(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst2 WITH t2 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: More than one RESOURCE
description:
A deployment drives one RESOURCE: each resource is its own execution unit, and the runtime scans on one thread.

A second resource used to compile at exit 0 and be refused at deploy; it is refused here instead, where it can be fixed.

This is a limit of the current runtime, not of the language; it lifts when multi-resource deployment lands.

title: TASK or PROGRAM outside a RESOURCE
description: A CONFIGURATION contains RESOURCE blocks; the tasks and the programs bound to them are declared inside one. Wrap them in `RESOURCE <name> ON <cpu> ... END_RESOURCE`.

title: Missing PRIORITY in TASK
description: PRIORITY is required in TASK configuration.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#20ms);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unusable TASK priority
description:
A TASK's `PRIORITY` must be a number the compiler can represent (a 32-bit unsigned integer), where 0 is the most urgent.

An unusable value would otherwise reach the scheduler as "no priority" and quietly sort last.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION cfg1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 99999999999);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: INTERVAL after PRIORITY in TASK
description: In a TASK configuration, INTERVAL must be declared before PRIORITY.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(PRIORITY := 1, INTERVAL := T#20ms);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: SINGLE after INTERVAL in TASK
description: In a TASK configuration, SINGLE must be declared before INTERVAL.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#20ms, SINGLE := var1, PRIORITY := 1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: SINGLE after PRIORITY in TASK
description: In a TASK configuration, SINGLE must be declared before PRIORITY.
sources:
CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(PRIORITY := 1, SINGLE := var1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unschedulable task
description: A TASK needs a cyclic INTERVAL to be scheduled. Event-driven forms (SINGLE) are not supported by the scan dispatcher.

title: Unknown TASK reference
description: The task name referenced in a `WITH` clause does not exist in this configuration.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH unknown_task : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Program instance without a task
description: Every program instance in a RESOURCE must be attached to a TASK with `WITH` - an unattached instance would never be scheduled.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR n : INT; END_VAR
    n := n + 1;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        PROGRAM P1 : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Configuration instance unknown
description: A `VAR_CONFIG` path references a program instance that does not exist.
sources:
PROGRAM MyProg
    VAR
        x : INT;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : MyProg;
    END_RESOURCE

    VAR_CONFIG
        noSuchInst.x : INT := 42;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Configuration field not found
description: A `VAR_CONFIG` path references a field that does not exist on the resolved type.
sources:
PROGRAM MyProg
    VAR
        x : INT;
    END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION MyCfg
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK t1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH t1 : MyProg;
    END_RESOURCE

    VAR_CONFIG
        inst1.nonexistent : INT := 42;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: VAR_ACCESS type mismatch
description: A `VAR_ACCESS` declaration's type does not match the referenced variable's actual type.
sources:
PROGRAM prog1
VAR
    my_var : INT;
END_VAR
VAR_ACCESS
    accessor : my_var : BOOL;
END_VAR
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION config1
    RESOURCE res1 ON CPU
        TASK task1(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM inst1 WITH task1 : prog1;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unsupported configuration element
description: Program connections (`inp := %IW1`) and per-FB task associations inside a program configuration are not supported.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_INPUT inp : INT; END_VAR
VAR n : INT; END_VAR
    n := inp;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P (inp := %IW1);
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Address cannot be located
description:
A directly represented variable (`%IX0.0`, `%QW4`) is storage in one of three bands: `%I`, `%Q` or `%M`. Written bare in a body, or bound with `AT` to a `VAR_GLOBAL` or to a PROGRAM's `VAR`, it is stored there, as part of a wider address when the program also names one.

Three kinds of address cannot be:

- An `AT` clause on a variable of a function, function block or class. Its variables belong to each call or instance, so one address cannot be theirs. Declare it in a PROGRAM, or as a `VAR_GLOBAL` of the CONFIGURATION, and name it from there. - A partly specified address, `%I*`. Its binding comes from `VAR_CONFIG`, which is checked but not applied yet (E1416). Write the address in full. - An address whose area or width letter is not one of `I`, `Q`, `M` and `X`, `B`, `W`, `D`, `L`, such as `%Z0` or `%IZ0`. A bit may leave its width out: `%I1` is `%IX1`.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK Valve
VAR
    POS AT %QW28 : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Unknown multibit access size
description:
A partial access names its width with `X`, `B`, `W`, `D` or `L`, in either case.

The grammar cannot reject any other letter, because it parses this position with the same rule as a direct variable's address, where `IX`, `QW` and `MD` are all legal.

An unrecognized size used to decode as no slice at all: the access typed as BOOL, `rk check` called it clean, and lowering then failed with an internal compiler error.

title: Write to an input location
description:
A variable declared `AT` an address in `%I` is part of the input image, which the host owns: it copies the process image into the input band before every scan.

A write the program makes is overwritten by that copy before anything can read it, so it is refused rather than accepted and silently lost.

Reading one is the whole point of an input and stays clean; `%Q` and `%M` may be written freely.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_EXTERNAL sensor : BOOL; END_VAR
    sensor := TRUE;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL sensor AT %IX0.0 : BOOL; END_VAR
    RESOURCE R ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: RETAIN on an I/O location
description:
The retain band is restored at startup, before the first scan.

Restoring an input or output image means that first scan runs on the values of the last power cycle, before the field bus has refreshed them — so `%I` and `%Q` cannot also be `RETAIN`.

`%M` is the area that may legitimately persist: it is the program's own, and no copy-in overwrites it.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_EXTERNAL sensor : BOOL; END_VAR
VAR seen : BOOL; END_VAR
    seen := sensor;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL RETAIN sensor AT %IX0.0 : BOOL; END_VAR
    RESOURCE R ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Duplicate location
description:
Two declarations are bound to the same address.

An address is one channel, but each declaration is given storage of its own, so the program would have two variables where the plant has one: a write through one is never seen through the other, and a host binding by address finds it twice.

Declare the channel once and name that variable wherever it is needed.

title: Location type mismatch
description:
A located variable holds one value as wide as its address, so it is declared as an elementary type of that width.

The size character says how wide the channel a host binds is: `X` one bit, `B` eight, `W` sixteen, `D` thirty-two, `L` sixty-four. Any elementary type of that width will do, so `%IW` takes a WORD, an INT or a UINT, and `%ID` a DWORD, a DINT or a REAL. An enum, a subrange, an ARRAY, a STRUCT or a STRING has no single width, and is refused: declare the elementary type and convert in the program.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR_EXTERNAL wide : INT; END_VAR
VAR t : INT; END_VAR
    t := wide;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
VAR_GLOBAL wide AT %IX0.0 : INT; END_VAR
    RESOURCE R ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Part of a wider address
description:
An address inside a wider one the program also names is part of it. Each size counts in its own units and the image is little-endian, so beside a `%QW0`, `%QX0.3` is its bit 3 and `%QB1` its high byte. A part is stored in the wider address's cell and has no storage of its own.

Reading a part, assigning it, and binding an output to it all work, and a declared part may have any type of its width. A part of a byte or more is whole bytes of the cell, so it can also be passed to a `VAR_IN_OUT` or referenced. The uses that need storage of its own do not work:

- passing a bit to a `VAR_IN_OUT`, or taking `REF()` of it, which both need an address a bit does not have; - counting a `FOR` loop with it; - declaring it `RETAIN` or giving it an initial value, which both belong on the variable located at the wider address.

title: Extern pragma outside a FUNCTION
description:
Only a FUNCTION lowers to a WASM import.

On a FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM or METHOD the pragma used to be silently ignored, leaving the body it stood on empty and the import never declared.

Wrap the import in a FUNCTION and call it from the block.
sources:
{extern 'host' 'fb-extern'}
FUNCTION_BLOCK Modbus
VAR_INPUT n : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Not representable on an extern FUNCTION
description:
An `{extern}` FUNCTION is a WASM import, and its interface is exactly its declaration: `VAR_INPUT` become the params (copies; aggregates as a pointer to a call-entry snapshot), scalar `VAR_OUTPUT` become the results in declaration order, and the return type is the last result.

Three things cannot cross that boundary: `VAR_IN_OUT` (a pointer into caller storage with a mutation contract; an extern takes copies), an aggregate or STRING output (no WASM result type to ride), and statements (the import IS the body).
sources:
{extern 'host' 'fill'}
FUNCTION fill : INT
VAR_IN_OUT buf : INT; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION

title: Test pragma outside a FUNCTION
description:
A {test} pragma is valid only on a FUNCTION, like {extern}: a test is a () entry the runner calls, and a FUNCTION_BLOCK, PROGRAM or METHOD has no such entry.

A POU that exists only for tests is hidden with FUNCTION PRIVATE, not marked as a test.

title: Wasm pragma outside a FUNCTION
description: Only FUNCTION bodies are scanned for a {wasm} intrinsic; anywhere else the pragma was silently dropped and the surrounding body compiled as if it were not there.

title: Unknown wasm instruction
description:
A {wasm} pragma names the instruction its body stands for, and the name must be one the emitter has an arm for.

An unknown name used to fall through to an unreachable trap (or, on the single-input conversion shape, to a silent identity) at exit 0.

title: Wasm operand not declared
description:
A {wasm} statement runs its instruction on the operands it names and writes the one its (result) names, so each must be a parameter, a local or the return of the FUNCTION.

An unknown name used to be ignored: the FUNCTION's own parameter list was lowered instead and the pragma's operands were decoration.

title: Wasm pragma operands do not fit the instruction
description:
Every operand of a {wasm} pragma pushes its wasm lane (i32, i64, f32 or f64; a STRING its pointer and length pair) and the instruction has a fixed signature.

A mismatch used to reach the module validator at load, from a compile that exited 0.

The message states what the instruction takes and what the pragma gives it.

title: Export pragma outside a FUNCTION
description:
An {export} pragma is valid only on a FUNCTION: it is the one POU a host can call with nothing but its parameters.

A PROGRAM is already exported, the schedule names it. A FUNCTION_BLOCK or a METHOD needs an instance, and the host does not have one.

Wrap the call in a FUNCTION and export that.
sources:
{export}
FUNCTION_BLOCK Motor
VAR_INPUT run : BOOL; END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: This FUNCTION cannot be exported
description:
An `{export}` FUNCTION is exported under its name, so it has to be one function with one name.

Five FUNCTIONs are not:

- an `{extern}` FUNCTION is an import, it has no body to export. - a `{test}` FUNCTION is already exported for `rk test`, and left out of a release build. - a FUNCTION that takes an interface is compiled once per implementation it is called with. - a variadic FUNCTION is compiled once per number of arguments it is called with. - an overloaded FUNCTION shares its name with the other overloads.

Export a plain FUNCTION that calls the one you wanted.

title: Info pragma notice
description: A call targets a POU annotated with `{info = '...'}`, providing an informational notice at the call site.
sources:
{info = 'prefer new_fn for better performance'}
FUNCTION old_fn : INT
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION caller : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    x := old_fn();
END_FUNCTION

title: Warning pragma notice
description: A call targets a POU annotated with `{warn = '...'}`, indicating deprecation or other warnings at the call site.
sources:
{warn = 'this function is deprecated, use fn2 instead'}
FUNCTION fn1 : INT
END_FUNCTION

FUNCTION caller : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    x := fn1();
END_FUNCTION

title: Invalid pragma for POU
description: A pragma that has no meaning on this POU kind: {once} on a PROGRAM. Placement of {test} and {extern} is a compiler error instead (E1503, E1501).

title: Once-function called multiple times
description: A function, function block, or method marked with `{once}` is called more than once in the same body. The `{once}` pragma indicates it should only be invoked once per execution cycle.

title: Unknown rule name in {allow}
description: An `{allow 'rule-name'}` pragma names a lint rule that does not exist, so it silences nothing. Rule names are the `[linter.rules]` names, e.g. `input-assignment`.

title: Unreachable code
description: A statement appears after an unconditional control flow statement (RETURN, EXIT, CONTINUE) and can never be reached.

title: Division by zero
description: A division or modulo operation uses a literal zero as the divisor.

title: Constant condition
description: A condition in an IF, WHILE, or REPEAT statement is always TRUE or always FALSE.

title: Self-assignment
description: A variable is assigned to itself, which has no effect.

title: Self-comparison
description: A variable is compared to itself. The result is always TRUE or always FALSE.

title: Subtraction from self
description: Subtracting a variable from itself always results in 0.

title: Identity operation
description: An operation with an identity value has no effect (adding 0, multiplying by 1, etc.).

title: Identical subexpressions
description: Both sides of a boolean operator are identical. This is likely a copy-paste error.

title: Duplicate CASE value
description: Two or more CASE branches use the same selector value. Only the first branch will ever match.

title: FOR loop step sign mismatch
description: The FOR loop step direction does not match the bounds direction.

title: Constant FOR loop bounds
description: A FOR loop has equal start and end bounds, so the body executes exactly once.

title: Loop variable modified
description: A FOR loop control variable is modified inside the loop body. This can cause unexpected iteration behavior.

title: Assignment to input variable
description: A `VAR_INPUT` variable is being assigned inside the POU body. Inputs are meant to be set by callers.

title: Missing return assignment
description: A function or method declares a return type but never assigns the return value.

title: Variable shadows its own POU
description: A variable has the same name as the function block, method, or program it is declared in.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK MyFB
VAR
    MyFB : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Method variable shadows an owner member
description:
A method's local or parameter has the same name as a member of the function block or class it belongs to.

This is legal — the method variable shadows the member and bare-name access resolves to the local — but it is easy to misread.

title: External instance mutation
description: A field of a function block or class instance is directly modified from outside. Instances should own their data.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK MyFB
VAR
    x : INT;
END_VAR
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION caller : INT
VAR
    fb : MyFB;
END_VAR
    fb.x := 42;
END_FUNCTION

title: Global accessed without VAR_EXTERNAL
description: A configuration VAR_GLOBAL is read directly by name. Strict IEC wants the program to import it explicitly with VAR_EXTERNAL.
sources:
PROGRAM P
VAR n : INT; END_VAR
    n := gCount;
END_PROGRAM

CONFIGURATION Cfg
    VAR_GLOBAL gCount : INT; END_VAR
    RESOURCE Res ON CPU
        TASK T(INTERVAL := T#10ms, PRIORITY := 1);
        PROGRAM P1 WITH T : P;
    END_RESOURCE
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Unused variable
description: A variable is declared but never used in the body.

title: Variable shadows POU
description: A variable name shadows a POU (function, function block, class, etc.) available in scope.
sources:
FUNCTION_BLOCK PrintLog
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

title: Duplicate variable section
description: The same variable section type (VAR, VAR_INPUT, etc.) appears more than once in a POU. Merge them into one.

title: Duplicate namespace
description: The same namespace is declared more than once in the same file. Merge them into one.
sources:
NAMESPACE Utils
    FUNCTION fn1 : INT
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

NAMESPACE Utils
    FUNCTION fn2 : INT
    END_FUNCTION
END_NAMESPACE

title: Duplicate configuration
description: Same-named CONFIGURATION blocks merge, which is how VAR_GLOBALs are split across files. Two in ONE file separate nothing — merge them.
sources:
CONFIGURATION Plant
    VAR_GLOBAL
        a : INT;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

CONFIGURATION Plant
    VAR_GLOBAL
        b : INT;
    END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

title: Uninitialized output
description: A `VAR_OUTPUT` variable is never assigned in the body. The instance field is zero-initialized, so this is permitted - but an output the body never writes is usually an unfinished one.

title: Negated condition
description: An `IF NOT ... THEN ... ELSE` can be simplified by swapping the branches and removing the negation.

title: Negated comparison
description: `NOT (x = y)` can be simplified to `x <> y`, and similar for other comparison operators.

title: Boolean comparison
description: A comparison with a boolean literal can be simplified. Use the variable directly or negate it.

title: Redundant NOT
description: A double negation (`NOT NOT x`) can be simplified to just `x`.

title: Unnecessary ELSE
description: The ELSE branch is unnecessary because all preceding IF/ELSIF branches end with RETURN, EXIT, or CONTINUE.

title: Single-element array
description: An array dimension has equal lower and upper bounds, resulting in an array with only one element.

title: Explicit default FOR step
description: `BY 1` is the default step - writing it out adds nothing.

title: Unused import
description: A `USING` directive imports a namespace that is never referenced.
sources:
NAMESPACE Tools
    FUNCTION_BLOCK Logger
    END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
END_NAMESPACE

title: Unused return value
description: A function call discards a return value. If the return value is intentionally ignored, assign it to a variable.

title: Missing input parameter
description:
A FUNCTION_BLOCK or PROGRAM call does not pass every declared `VAR_INPUT`.

This is not an error - the instance keeps the input's previous value - but an unwired input is usually an oversight.

A FUNCTION call that omits an input is the hard error E0802 instead.

title: CASE without ELSE
description: A CASE statement has no ELSE branch, which may leave unhandled cases.

title: Empty body
description: A function, function block, method, or program has an empty body.
sources:
FUNCTION compute : INT
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty IF branch
description: An IF or ELSIF branch has no statements.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR
    x : BOOL;
END_VAR
    IF x THEN
    END_IF;
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty CASE branch
description: A CASE branch has no statements, which may indicate a missing implementation.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    CASE x OF
        1:
        2: test := 20;
    END_CASE;
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty loop body
description: A FOR, WHILE, or REPEAT loop has no statements in its body.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR
    i : INT;
END_VAR
    FOR i := 0 TO 10 DO
    END_FOR;
END_FUNCTION

title: Empty type declaration
description: A STRUCT has no fields or an ENUM has no variants.

title: Effectless statement
description: A statement has no side effects and does nothing.

title: Unnecessary parentheses
description: Parentheses around a simple variable or literal have no effect and can be removed.
sources:
FUNCTION test : INT
VAR x : INT; END_VAR
    test := (x);
END_FUNCTION

title: Collapsible IF
description: Two nested IF statements without ELSE branches can be collapsed into a single `IF a AND b THEN`.

title: Yoda condition
description: A literal value appears on the left side of a comparison. Swap operands for conventional order.
